premise: At 58 I paid off my brother-in-law’s $95,000 second mortgage on his farm after he signed a notarized contract giving me a life estate in the east wing and inheritance of the entire property; he refinanced, pulled $200,000 in equity, sold the farm to a developer, and handed me a $10,000 check with a 30‑day eviction notice—I sued with a recorded video of his promise, the court voided the sale, and I now own the farm, lease the back acres to a pumpkin patch called 'Gourd of Deceit,' and require him to work the register in a scarecrow outfit with a badge that reads 'Financially Plowed.'
